spots.name: Independence Palace
spots.summary: The Independence Palace, also publicly and officially known as the Reunification Convention Hall or simply Reunification Hall, is a historic landmark and government-owned public hall in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.

spots.name: Landmark 81
spots.summary: Landmark 81 is a supertall skyscraper in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. It is primarily invested in and developed by Vinhomes, the largest Vietnamese real-estate developer.

spots.name: Saigon Notre-Dame Basilica

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica of Saigon, officially the Cathedral Basilica of Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception is a cathedral located in the Saigon ward of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.

spots.name: Bitexco Financial Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Bitexco Financial Tower is a skyscraper in Financial District, Saigon, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. At its completion in 2010, it became the tallest building in Vietnam and kept this status until January 2011, when it was surpassed by Keangnam Hanoi Landmark Tower.

names.ja: ビテクスコ・フィナンシャルタワー

spots.name: Saigon Zoo and Botanical Gardens
spots.summary: The Saigon Zoo and Botanical Gardens, or locally and coloquially known as The Zoo, is Vietnam's oldest zoo and botanical garden.

names.nl: Dierentuin en botanische tuin van Saigon
names.fr: Jardin botanique et zoologique de Saigon

spots.name: War Remnants Museum
spots.summary: The War Remnants Museum is a war museum at 28 Võ Văn Tần Street, Xuân Hòa, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. It contains exhibits relating to the First Indochina War and the Vietnam War.

names.es: Museo de los Vestigios de la Guerra de Vietnam

spots.name: Bến Thành Market
spots.summary: Bến Thành Market is located in the center of Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon), Vietnam in District 1. The market is one of the earliest surviving structures in the city and an important symbol of the city. Ben Thanh Market is a famous destination for many local and foreign tourists from all around the world.

spots.name: Xá Lợi Pagoda

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Xá Lợi Pagoda is the largest pagoda in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. It was built in 1956 and was the headquarters of Buddhism in South Vietnam. The pagoda is located in District 3, Ho Chi Minh City and lies on a plot of 5000 square metres.

spots.name: Ho Chi Minh City Museum of Fine Arts

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Ho Chi Minh City Museum of Fine Arts is the major art museum of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, and second in the country only to the Vietnam National Museum of Fine Arts in Hanoi.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Ho Chi Minh City Museum of Fine Arts

names.es: Museo de Bellas Artes de Ciudad Ho Chi Minh

spots.name: Saigon Centre
spots.summary: Saigon Centre is a mixed-use complex in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, invested by Keppel Land Watco, a joint-venture among Keppel Land from Singapore with both Vietnamese companies Real Estate Saigon Corporation (RESCO) and Southern Waterborne Transport Corporation (SOWATCO).

spots.name: Dragon House
spots.summary: Dragon House or Dragon House Wharf, Dragon House Harbour, officially known as Ho Chi Minh Museum, Ho Chi Minh City Branch, was the original commercial port of Saigon. The construction began in 1862 and more than a year later, in 1863, the house was completed.

spots.name: Saigon Opera House
spots.summary: Saigon Opera House is a municipal opera house in downtown Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Like other French-built opera houses during French colonial period, including Hanoi Opera House and Haiphong Opera House, it is an example of French Colonial architecture in Vietnam.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Ho Chi Minh City Opera House

names.fr: Théâtre municipal de Hô Chi Minh-Ville

spots.name: Museum of Ho Chi Minh City

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Museum of Ho Chi Minh City, formerly known as Gia Long Palace (Vietnamese: Dinh Gia Long), is a historical site and museum in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. The museum is situated at the corner of Lý Tự Trọng and Nam Kỳ Khởi Nghĩa streets, located on a 2-hectare block near the Independence Palace.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Museum of Ho Chi Minh City

spots.name: Đồng Khởi Street
spots.summary: Đồng Khởi Street, formerly known as Rue Catinat then Tự Do Street, is a street in Saigon, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.

spots.name: Ho Chi Minh City Museum of History

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Ho Chi Minh City Museum of History is located at 2 Nguyễn Bỉnh Khiêm, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Formerly known as the Musée Blanchard de la Brosse, and The National Museum of Vietnam in Saigon, it received its current name in 1979.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Ho Chi Minh City Museum of History

names.fr: Musée d’histoire de Hô Chi Minh-Ville
names.es: Museo de Historia de la ciudad de Ho Chi Minh

spots.name: Bình Tây Market

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Bình Tây Market is the largest market in Chợ Lớn; located in Bình Tây ward, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Prior to 1975, it was also referred to as "Chợ Lớn mới". to differentiate from its predecessor, "Chợ Lớn cũ".

spots.name: Hùng King Temple

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Hùng King Temple is a temple dedicated to the Hùng kings, the Vietnamese rulers of the Hồng Bàng dynasty. The temple is located in the Saigon Zoo and Botanical Gardens, next to the Ho Chi Minh City Museum of History.

spots.name: Thien Hau Temple

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Thiên Hậu Temple, officially the Tuệ Thành Assembly Hall is a Chinese-style temple of the Chinese Goddess of Sea, Mazu on Nguyễn Trãi Street in the Chợ Lớn ward of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.

spots.name: Bạch Đằng Quay
spots.summary: Bạch Đằng Quay is a wharf and park with an address No.2 Tôn Đức Thắng Boulevard, Bến Nghé, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. It stretches along about 1.3 kilometres (0.81 mi) of the Saigon River from the Thủ Ngữ flagpole to the site of the former Ba Son Shipyard and covers an area of 23,400 square metres (252,000 sq ft).

spots.name: Bùi Viện Street
spots.summary: Bùi Viện Street is a small street in Bến Thành, Ho Chi Minh City. This is the city's famous nightlife street with many small bars and beer gardens, specializing in affordable tourist goods and services.

spots.name: Nguyễn Huệ Boulevard
spots.summary: Nguyễn Huệ Boulevard is a boulevard in District 1, downtown Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Being one of Saigon's oldest thoroughfares, the boulevard has undergone several transformations; it is currently a famous pedestrian street in the city.

spots.name: Citadel of Saigon
spots.summary: The Citadel of Saigon also known as the Citadel of Gia Định was a late 18th-century fortress that stood in Saigon, Vietnam from its construction in 1790 until its destruction in February 1859.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Tân Định Church or Tân Định Parish Church is a Roman Catholic church in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Its formal name is the Church of the Sacred Heart of Jesus.

spots.name: Vietcombank Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Vietcombank Tower is a skyscraper in Ho Chi Minh City. It is 205 m (673 ft) tall and has a floor area of 3,232m2 and has 35 above ground floors and 4 underground floors.

spots.name: Giác Lâm Temple

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Giác Lâm Temple is a historic Buddhist temple in Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon), the largest city in Vietnam. Built in 1744, it is one of the oldest temples in the city.

spots.name: Jade Emperor Pagoda

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Jade Emperor Pagoda also known as the Phước Hải Tự is a Taoist, Buddhist, Confucian pagoda located at District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. It was founded by a Chinese merchant named Liu Daoyuan, a Cantonese migrant. It is also known from 1984 by the new Buddhist name Phước Hải Tự. Then U.S.

spots.name: Mê Linh Square
spots.summary: Mê Linh Square is a city square next to the Saigon River in Saigon ward, downtown Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. The square has a semi-circular shape and features a statue of Trần Hưng Đạo, it is separated from the Saigon River by the Bạch Đằng Quay.

spots.name: Paris Commune Square
spots.summary: Paris Commune Square is a small square and roundabout located in Saigon ward, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. It lies between Lê Duẩn Boulevard and Nguyễn Du Street and surrounds the Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica of Saigon. This is also the starting point of the famous Đồng Khởi Street.

spots.name: Vinh Nghiem Pagoda

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Vĩnh Nghiêm Pagoda is a pagoda in an area of 6,000 square metres (65,000 sq ft) at 339, Nam Kỳ Khởi Nghĩa street, Ward 7, District 3 Ho Chi Minh City. This is the first pagoda in Vietnam to be built in Vietnamese traditional architecture style but with concrete.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Vĩnh Nghiêm Pagoda, Ho Chi Minh City

spots.name: Mariamman Temple, Ho Chi Minh City

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Mariamman Temple in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, is a temple dedicated to the Hindu goddess Mariamman. It was built in the late 19th century by the Nagarathar a trade community from Tamil Nadu, India.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Mariamman Temple, Ho Chi Minh City

spots.name: Quách Thị Trang Square
spots.summary: Quách Thị Trang Square is the city square in front of the well-known Bến Thành Market in District 1, downtown Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon), Vietnam.

spots.name: Lê Duẩn Boulevard
spots.summary: Lê Duẩn Boulevard is a boulevard in District 1, downtown Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. The boulevard stretches from Nam Kỳ Khởi Nghĩa Street, right across from the Independence Palace, across the April 30 Park, to Nguyễn Bỉnh Khiêm Street, right across from the Saigon Zoo and Botanical Gardens.

spots.name: Lam Sơn Square
spots.summary: Lam Sơn Square is the city square surrounding the Municipal Theatre of Ho Chi Minh City in Downtown Saigon, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.

spots.name: Phạm Ngũ Lão Street
spots.summary: Phạm Ngũ Lão Street is a street in Bến Thành, Ho Chi Minh City, formerly Saigon, Vietnam. It was named after Phạm Ngũ Lão, a general of the Trần dynasty.

spots.name: Tôn Đức Thắng Boulevard
spots.summary: Tôn Đức Thắng Boulevard is a thoroughfare in District 1, Downtown Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.

spots.name: Lê Lợi Boulevard
spots.summary: Lê Lợi Boulevard is a boulevard in District 1, downtown Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. The boulevard stretches from Đồng Khởi Street, right across from Lam Sơn Square to the Quách Thị Trang Square and directly connects to Trần Hưng Đạo Boulevard to go to Chợ Lớn.

spots.name: Thủ Thiêm Bridge
spots.summary: Thủ Thiêm Bridge is a 6-lane bridge in Ho Chi Minh City, the largest city of Vietnam, opened in 2008. The bridge links District 2 with Bình Thạnh District, near downtown District 1. This bridge is an important link between existing downtown of Ho Chi Minh City with Thu Thiem New Urban Area.

spots.name: Saigon Times Square

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Saigon Times Square or Times Square Saigon, simply as Times Square, is a high-rise building in Bến Nghé, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. This building is a 40-storey joint tower and features a modern architectural style.

spots.name: Tao Đàn Park
spots.summary: Tao Đàn Park or fully known as Tao Đàn Cultural Park, also known as Tao Đàn Garden is an urban park in District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam behind the Independence Palace with an address 55C Nguyễn Thị Minh Khai, Bến Thành. It is one of the largest parks in the city, covering 10 hectares.

spots.name: April 30 Park
spots.summary: April 30 Park is a park located in the center of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, within District 1 facing Independence Palace and behind Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica of Saigon.

spots.name: Đầm Sen Park

hours.note: Closed Tue, Sun

spots.summary: Dam Sen Cultural Park is an amusement park located in Bình Thới ward, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. The park has an area of 50 hectares, of which 20% comprises lakes and 60% trees and gardens.

spots.name: Turtle Lake
spots.summary: Turtle Lake is a lake and a fountain surrounded by a traffic roundabout officially known as International Square in District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.

spots.name: Saigon Central Mosque
spots.summary: The Saigon Central Mosque is a mosque in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam and it is one of the ancient and historic Mosque in the region.

spots.name: Quan Am Temple
spots.summary: The Ôn Lăng Assembly Hall, also known as the Quan Âm Temple (Chùa Quân Âm), is a Chinese-style Buddhist temple located on Lão Tử Street in Chợ Lớn ward, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.

spots.name: Bến Thành Theatre
spots.summary: Bến Thành Theatre is a theatre for performing arts inside a building that technically known as District 1 Cultural Center, now is Saigon Ward Public Service Center. Located at No.

spots.name: Hàm Nghi Boulevard
spots.summary: Hàm Nghi Boulevard is an east–west boulevard in District 1, central district of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. The boulevard stretches from Tôn Đức Thắng Boulevard to the Quách Thị Trang Square. The thoroughfare is also part of the Financial District, Saigon.

spots.name: September 23rd Park
spots.summary: September 23rd Park, or written as 23/9 Park, is a 9 ha park in Bến Thành, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City.

spots.name: Mong Bridge
spots.summary: The Mong Bridge is a steel bridge across the Bến Nghé Channel, connecting District 1 and District 4 of Ho Chi Minh City. It is one of the oldest bridges in that city.

spots.summary: The General Sciences Library of Ho Chi Minh City is a Vietnamese public library. It is run by the Department of Culture and Sports of Ho Chi Minh City. The library's main functions are to collect, preserve and organise library resources.

spots.name: Chi Lăng Park
spots.summary: Chi Lăng Park is a park located in the heart of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, within the jurisdiction of District 1. It was named after the Battle of Chi Lăng in Lạng Sơn province.

spots.summary: Bách Tùng Diệp Park is a park situated in the heart of Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon), Vietnam, within District 1. It is surrounded by streets of Lý Tự Trọng, Nam Kỳ Khởi Nghĩa, and Pasteur. It is opposite the City Museum and covering an area of approximately 5,000 square metres,

spots.summary: Thống Nhất Stadium, formerly Cộng Hoà Stadium is the second-largest multi-purpose stadium in Ho Chi Minh City, and the oldest in Vietnam. It is located on 138 Đào Duy Từ Street, Diên Hồng.

spots.name: The Geological Museum of Vietnam

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: A rare gem and a must see for geology & natural history enthusiasts. This 3-story building houses a collection of earthly artifacts (and even some non-earthly ones), including a few rare examples. Sadly in a state of neglect with poor lighting and little to no interpretive text. You can read more about it [https://saigoneer.com/in-plain-sight/18294-in-defense-of-b%E1%BA%A3o-t%C3%A0ng-%C4%91%E1%BB%

spots.name: The Venerable Thich Quảng Đức Monument
spots.summary: A monument dedicated to the Buddhist monk Thich Quảng Đức, who self-immolated at the site in 1963 in protest against the persecution of South Vietnam's Buddhist majority by the Roman Catholic-dominated Ngô Đình Diệm government.

spots.name: Acoustic Cafe

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Though only 1 km from the heavily touristed centre, this club is completely outside the tourist orbit, and offers an interesting view of local life. The all-Vietnamese house band performs every night, mostly American music, and it's always jammed with student-aged groupies. For some reason, they address the crowd in English between songs, even though half the crowd doesn't understand. On weekends,

spots.name: Quan An Ngon

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Two different restaurants operate with the same name within a few blocks of each other, one at 160 Pasteur Street, and the other on Nam Ky Khoi Nghia across from the Reunification Palace. Set in atmospheric old French villas, with similar menus Vietnamese food, including regional specialities prepared in numerous independently-operated food stalls around the perimeter. Both are popular and both te

spots.name: Go2 Bar
spots.summary: The main backpacker bar while Allez Boo was closed, still a great meeting place. It's impossible to miss the four floors of neon lights on the outside. Large patio on the sidewalk at street level, a cosier bar on the second floor with occasional live music or big-screen sports, plus a rooftop patio (with retractable roof) with individual BBQs up a steep set of stairs on the 5th floor.

spots.name: Le Pub

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Always busy after 18:00, famous for its strong drinks, daily dollar-specials (e.g., Tuesday USD1 for vodka mixers all night) and friendly staff. It has the same owner as Le Pub in Hanoi. The Pub Quiz (almost every Tuesday) is very popular with expats, especially the English teachers. Get there early or it's too packed to find a place to sit down. Indoors and outdoor tables available.

spots.name: Allez Boo

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: For those who have been here before, you'll find the original bar is now Highlands Coffee and an all new Allez Boo has opened on the opposite corner. It's shiny and brand-new, but retains the same feel as the original. There's a bar with air-con on the 2nd floor with DJ-type music, and an airy rooftop patio. Quite similar to its sibling establishment, Go2 Bar.

spots.name: Rex Hotel Rooftop

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: They serve a buffet dinner at the dinner hour, which gradually gives way to drinks and music. Acts change over time, but have included a Filipino band playing FM classics and a Vietnamese group playing Latin and flamenco. It's a pleasant place to get above the city noise and enjoy some fresh air. Cocktails around 140,000 dong.

spots.name: Bloom Saigon Restaurant
spots.summary: Temporarily closed as of August 2022. Non-profit restaurant run by Aid to Children Without Parents (ACWP) and serves as a culinary training facility. Very nice staff, excellent food, terrace on the 3rd floor. Situated a bit in the North and in a small calm community. Worth to go by foot, 20 mnin walk from the Jade Pagoda.

spots.name: Alibi

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Very cosy atmosphere, with sofas lining the walls and beautiful decor. Good food & drinks selection, nice music, and a mix of both locals & expats. Friendly staff, and the management's always there to make you feel welcome and make sure you get what you are asking for.

spots.name: ZanZBar

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Casual-upscale, the clients tend to come for the great choice of wines-by-the-glass (huge walk-in wine cellar), or for the cocktails (premium brands) and good selection of imported beers. Can remain open after midnight, depending on the number of customers.

spots.name: Pho Quynh

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Their specialty is pho. Locals come regularly and lucky backpackers stumble upon it. It is air-conditioned on the second and third floors. They also have decent banh mi bo kho, which is beef stew with carrots, served with French baguette.

spots.name: Apocalypse Now

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Legendary and still packed on weekends, although aside from a few movie references it's not all that much to look at. Stays open late. Now opened their 2nd floor for DJ, dancing, drinks with less crowded atmosphere.

spots.name: Hoa Khai Vegetarian Restaurant

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Tasty Vietnamese vegetarian food although with surly service. Be careful of being charged for unexpected items, such as the disposable hand towels that are presented to you without asking as you sit down.

spots.name: Hủ Tiếu Hồng Phát

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Restaurant selling Hủ tiếu Nam Vang, a flat rice noodle dish that is a specialty of the city. The dish is often called "Cambodian noodles" in English, even though it cannot be found in Cambodia.

spots.name: Anan Saigon

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A premier fine dining restaurant in Ho Chi Minh City, one of only two in Vietnam to be ranked among Asia's top 50 restaurants. Reservations essential.

spots.name: Bi Saigon

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Extensive menu with a choice between Vietnamese, Italian, Mexican and other styles. Open plan kitchen so you can see your food being prepared.

spots.name: Bún Chả 145

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Typical restaurant in the most amazing street of the city. Very good place for Bun Cha. As of February 2026, it is closed for renovation.

spots.name: Nhà Hàng Chay Ngọc Thọ

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Incredible range of delicoius veggie options, but also meat and chicken. Clean place, friendly staff, tasty food and satisfying portions.

spots.name: Nhà Hàng Asian Kitchen

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Very good place for delicious and diverse food, big choice. Kinda hidden, kinda great. Also lots of vegetarian options.

spots.name: Bánh Mì 37

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Absolutely delicious even though a bit different than the traditional. Popular among locals, there might be a queue.

spots.name: The Lunch Lady
spots.summary: The famous Lunch Lady was featured on Anthony Bourdain's show. Different noodle dish every day.
